name: Vareth Mango-Cardamom Hard Drops
description: Machine-formed hard candy drops in a translucent amber-gold, combining alphonso-style synth-mango with warm cardamom that intensifies as the candy dissolves. Sold in resealable tins of thirty.
flavor_profile: Intensely sweet synth-mango up front, building cardamom warmth mid-dissolve, clean finish with no chemical aftertaste
slogan: Thirty pieces. All of them good.
cultural_context: Vareth drops are ubiquitous — found in every waiting room, transit hub, and office break station in Meridian 88. They're considered almost invisible, the background candy that everyone has eaten but no one thinks about. That ubiquity makes them deeply trusted by Tier 1-3 users who can't afford to gamble on unknown brands, but slightly embarrassing to be caught eating above Tier 3.
story_hooks: Vareth Consumer Group has been adding a trace compound to its hard drops for years — not harmful, but flagged in a leaked internal audit as a 'preference reinforcement agent' that makes users slightly more likely to repurchase.
A Tier 5 executive's child was caught with a tin of Vareth drops — the scandal isn't the candy, it's what it implies about where the child has been spending time.
A specific tin batch number has been circulating as a signal among Shelf dissidents — anyone carrying Tin Batch 7-Amber is safe to talk to.
